title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Positive Psychology and Stress Management Interventions for Test Anxiety and Test-Related Stress
summary: Situations in which an evaluation of performance takes place - such as in an examination situation - can cause enormous anxiety and stress, up to and including pronounced test anxiety. Examination situations evoke cognitive appraisals of the situation and of oneself occur, as well as further psychophysiological reactions. Individuals with higher test anxiety show higher psychophysiologicial reactivity to exams and tend to perform poorer in exams. In the planned study, the effectiveness of a conventional cognitive-behavioral intervention (stress management training) and a positive-psychological intervention will be investigated in students as compared to a waiting control group with regard to a reduction of test anxiety and test-related stress in real exam situations. The effectiveness of the interventions will be measured using self-assessment questionnaires and psychophysiological stress markers.
conditions: test anxiety and test related stress

Waiting control group: the waiting control group consists of students who do not receive any intervention between two real written exams. Apart from this, they will undergo the same measurements as the two intervention groups.
General control condition: all students go through the same procedure as an exam day (all measurements) on an exam-free day as a control condition, without a stress condition.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Students who have at least two written exams remaining.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe depressive episodes, suicidality, participants currently undergoing psychotherapeutic treatment, participants taking medication.
